"Hunt Treasure on Site of Old Town / Hermit's Gold is Sought as Last Vestige of Jennings Goes", Ann Arbor Times News, 8 Jun 1923, p. 15 (AP); also Coldwater Daily Reporter, 9 Jun 1923, p. 5 (Newspapers.com 1370378882), and Flint Journal, 17 Jun 1923 (GenealogyBank)
"Hunt Now On In Town of Jennings", Flint Journal, 17 Jun 1923, p. 6 (AP; fullest wire copy)
Missaukee County atlas 1906, Lake Twp plate (Ancestry)
set.t: One 1923 wire story; the Cadillac papers are not indexed for 1923. Old Jennings Cemetery (south of the village) is graves: look-only. The hermit is not yet identified. The 1910 census of Lake Twp lists only one Swedish-born Larson, Lewis Larson (born 1851) and his wife Matilda; no John or Jens Larson appears in Missaukee Co. in 1900 or 1910. A Jens Larson who died in Lake Twp in 1916 was a Danish-born farmer and does not fit. The 1906 plat shows one L. G. Larson 40 in sec. 24, 3 mi SE of the village and away from the lakes; no proven link to the hermit. Pin stays on the village and Crooked Lake.
set.tovw: Lead grade D: one 1923 wire story in several papers and no local original; the hermit is not identified in the census or on the plat; the son's search and the church-site guess are rumour; no find reported.
